name: Private credit stress
value: BDC exits above 5% caps; OBDC ~25% below NAV
summary: Nontraded BDC redemption requests stay above usual 5% caps and listed BDCs trade at wide discounts; no wave of gates
state: Client redemptions from nontraded BDCs reached $12.7bn in the first half of 2026, and Blackstone's BCRED received second-quarter requests of about 10% of shares, double the usual 5% limit (InvestmentNews, 18 Nov). Blue Owl Capital Corporation traded about 25% below its reported NAV on 5 Nov (Finimize). Searches on 27 Nov found no simultaneous gating by several large funds, no forced asset sales and no losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Most exposed are investors in nontraded BDCs and semi-liquid private credit funds, whose withdrawals can be limited to about 5% a quarter. Mid-sized companies that borrow from private lenders may face tighter terms if stress builds.
rubric_hit: Watch: redemptions above 5% limits and listed BDCs at wide discounts to NAV (~25%); no multi-fund gating or forced sales

sources.title: InvestmentNews — After a tough year, are private credit funds and BDCs in line for a comeback in 2027?
Finimize — Blue Owl's shares trade a quarter below reported NAV

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
